app._comment: Static PWA (index.html at repo root, no build step, no root package.json). Served with `python -m http.server 8080` from the repo root; gate.py never starts this itself (checked: nothing in gate.py reads app.start), so the operator running the gate must have that server already up at app.url before running the e2e/a11y_ux domains, or those two will fail closed with connection errors rather than reporting real findings. This local server does NOT apply the repo's `_headers` file (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, etc.) -- those only apply on Cloudflare Pages -- so header-dependent checks here understate what production actually sends. Routes are hash-based SPA routes read from route() in index.html, not guessed: '/' defaults to today's or the latest post; /#/map, /#/ladder, /#/kodex, /#/discover are fixed views; /#/doc/{slug} fetches corpus/{slug}.md (only ai-pr-review and mcp-sensitive-data exist on disk today); /#/2026-07-25 pins a specific day's post and will need updating as the daily post rotates -- it is largely redundant with '/' (same view type) and can be dropped or re-pinned in a later edit without weakening coverage, since '/' already exercises the daily-post view.

unit._waiver_history: WAIVED 2026-07-27 on a WRONG diagnosis, LIFTED 2026-07-29. The waiver claimed the daemon was not running. It was: pid 9784 had held :8788 since 2026-07-22, answering /health 200 and a bare GET 401. The real fault was POST /chat returning 500 from a week-old process whose Claude Agent SDK runtime had gone stale. Restarting it fixed the domain: 10 pass, 0 fail. Two lessons kept here rather than in a commit message. First, 'connection refused' was assumed and never measured; `curl -m 8 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:8788/health` would have cost nothing. Second, the daemon wrote its stderr nowhere, so the 500 had no trace; it now appends to state/_daemon.log, which is how the restart was confirmed.
unit._comment: Runs the whole tests/ directory as of 2026-07-29; it was pinned to tests/boundaries.test.ts back when that was the only file, which meant a new test file would sit in the repo and never gate anything. Measured 2026-07-29: 22 pass, 0 fail, 35 expect() calls across 2 files. tests/mentor.test.ts is pure logic, hermetic, ~60ms: it lifts the המנטור queue block out of index.html and evaluates it, because the app is one inline script with no module boundary and a hand-copied fixture would drift. It carries a regression oracle for the suppression bug found the same day (a belief is keyed semantically, so suppression must match belief.from, not the belief id; proven to fail against the previous logic before the fix). tests/boundaries.test.ts is NOT hermetic and the gate must not be read as if it were: it makes an authenticated, state-mutating (self-restoring) round trip against the LIVE production Cloudflare Worker at https://sadna-sync.shovalb9.workers.dev, and 4 of its 10 tests require a local daemon answering on http://localhost:8788 (started separately via `cd daemon && bun run server.ts`). If that daemon is not running when the gate executes, those 4 fail closed with connection-refused rather than being skipped. COVERAGE BOUNDARY: this domain is example-based and integration only. There is no property-based, mutation, fuzz or contract testing anywhere in this repo, and the gate has no domain for any of them; filed 2026-07-29 to claude-setup as a gap against work-docs/testing_practices.txt section 6.

types.cmd: node --check sw.js && python tools/check_inline_js.py && python -m compileall -q tools && bash -n tools/gen_art.sh && python tools/check_callsites.py --selftest && python tools/check_callsites.py
types._comment:
No tsconfig, .eslintrc, or biome.json anywhere in the repo outside daemon/'s node_modules dependencies, so there is no real typecheck or lint to run -- this is a syntax-only sweep of every piece of JS/shell in the deployed app: sw.js (the only standalone JS file since tree3d.js was deleted on 2026-08-07 as dead code; `node --check tree3d.js` was in this command and failed on node 18 with SyntaxError on `export`, because the file was an ES module and node checks a .js as CommonJS, so the dead file was breaking a required domain), the ~137KB inline <script> block in index.html (the bulk of the app's logic, extracted and checked by the new tools/check_inline_js.py helper added alongside this contract -- see that file for the extraction method), every tools/*.py file via compileall, and the one shell tool script. It catches parse errors, nothing semantic. Personally run 2026-07-25 via the exact shell (subprocess.run(..., shell=True) on Windows, i.e. cmd.exe) that gate.py itself uses: exit 0, 'inline script #0 (113134 bytes): ok' plus clean compileall and bash -n.

EXTENDED 2026-08-10 with tools/check_callsites.py, because everything above this line is a PARSE check and there is a whole defect class it cannot see. A cut that removes a function's last call site leaves syntactically valid JS, so `node --check` exits 0 and check_inline_js.py prints ok; the container is markup so a DOM assertion still finds it; and the feature silently stops rendering. Measured against this repo's own history rather than argued: 8a917e3 orphaned counters() in writing/the-bench.html (3 references before, 0 after, definition untouched) and it stayed broken through 2008446 until e79d5b4 restored the two calls, which is the entire window in which the operator was asked to review that page. `check_callsites.py --base 8a917e3^ --head 8a917e3` exits 1 on that pair and `--base 2008446 --head e79d5b4` exits 0, both run 2026-08-10. The check is delta-based on purpose: an absolute 'every function needs a caller' rule would go red on genuinely dead code mid-removal and on a definition added before its caller, and --selftest asserts both of those false-positive shapes stay green alongside the planted red case. It grades the working tree against HEAD, or HEAD~1..HEAD when the tree is clean, since the gate runs after the final commit and a clean-tree diff would otherwise be green by construction. Exit 2 means it could not measure (no git, unreadable ref) rather than that it failed, per this file's own convention. Also added to .github/workflows/ci.yml, which needs fetch-depth 2 for HEAD~1 to exist.

RENEWED 2026-08-24 WITH FIXES LANDED, NOT UNCHANGED. The waiver lapsed on 2026-08-15 and nothing noticed for nine days, which is itself a finding (nothing watches waived.until). What changed this renewal: setTab() now sets aria-current=page on the active tab and the ladder arm chips carry aria-pressed, so the two idempotent-control findings (the exact accessibility gap this waiver's previous version named) are addressed at the root; verified live via getComputedStyle/getAttribute on a fresh render, aria-current=page present. The three /#/discover positional-selector findings are a harness-side control-identity limitation (the cards already carry data-id; flow.py addresses them positionally), filed for lane A rather than papered over here. Falsifier for this renewal: a cold-profile flow.py audit run from PowerShell per this domain's own operating instruction, expected to show the two tab findings gone; if they persist, the aria fix was not what the checker measures and this waiver must not be renewed again on the same reasoning. PRIOR REASON KEPT BELOW.

CORRECTED 2026-08-08 AFTER A/B'ING THE BROWSER CACHE. Every number in the previous three versions of this waiver was measured through a long-lived Chrome session that was serving STALE CSS, and the conclusions drawn from them were wrong. flow.py never calls Network.setCacheDisabled, so an audit session that has been alive across a CSS edit grades the old stylesheet. Re-measured against a brand new Chrome profile, same command, same 8 routes, same commit:

  warm session (wrong):  28 fail =  4 flow + 21 target + 3 contrast
  cold profile (true):    6 fail =  6 flow +  0 target + 0 contrast

The tap-target and contrast failures are GONE, not unmeasured. 34 target warns and 5 contrast warns remain, all inside the comfortable band above the WCAG floor rather than violations. The previous version of this waiver stated flatly that 'contrast did not move at all despite a pass aimed at it' and called that an open unexplained gap. That claim was an artifact of my own browser cache and is withdrawn.

THE NON-DETERMINISM IS STILL REAL and is not the same thing as the cache. Three warm runs gave 40, 28 and 15 failures, and the 15-fail run produced ZERO target and ZERO contrast findings across all 8 routes: those checks found nothing to measure because the page had not rendered, so an unloaded page scores CLEANER than a healthy one. Two confirm strings died to this inside one session, '(40 fail)' at 39 and a specific Hebrew contrast finding at zero-contrast-findings.

WHAT REMAINS, all 6 of them flow findings, each driven individually over CDP: the #flat2d tree tab and #tab-kodex are CORRECTLY idempotent, pressed while already active, measured at delta 0 with nodes 424 to 424 across 3 trials each; neither sets aria-current, so the no-op is invisible to a screen reader, which is a real accessibility gap rather than a flow one. The /#/ladder details summary could not be reproduced as dead in 5 isolated trials that each moved innerText by 1251 characters. The three /#/discover findings are positional selectors over cards that rotate every run, so that selector is not a stable identity for a control.

The confirm string is #tab-kodex, deterministic by construction: an anchor to the route the audit is already on cannot fire hashchange and cannot change the DOM. It survives cold and warm runs alike, which the two previous confirm strings did not.

RENEWED 2026-08-24, AND THE DOMINANT WARN CLASS IS FIXED, NOT EXEMPTED. Operator decision this date: deal with the text-size warns, do not carve them out of the oracle. Done at the root: every sub-.75rem font-size declaration in style.css (18 of them: .58/.6/.62/.66/.68/.7/.72/.74rem), the 10.5px #ring SVG text, and the browser-default <small> in .sy-t rows floored to 12px. Verified against a live render after a hard reload, not against the stale report: a getComputedStyle sweep of every text-bearing element across all six routes (/, map, ladder, kodex, discover, history) returns ZERO elements under 12px. The 313 text warns in state/e2e/last.json describe the pre-fix stylesheet; the report is now stale by construction and a cold-profile flow.py re-audit is the falsifier. What remains for that re-audit to size: 28-34 target warns and 5 contrast warns previously measured in the comfortable band above the WCAG floor, and 8 layout warns. max_warn stays 0 until the re-audit yields a measured ratchet number instead of a guessed budget. Still deliberately deferred, still named so it is not lost: the .finish-day gradient needs its --btn-face pass with screenshot review under DESIGN.md. PRIOR REASON KEPT BELOW.

CORRECTED 2026-08-08. This domain reads state/e2e/last.json against max_warn 0, and the previous version of this waiver reported 21 tap-target and 3 contrast FAILURES that do not exist. They were an artifact of a long-lived Chrome session serving stale CSS; flow.py never calls Network.setCacheDisabled. Re-measured on a cold browser profile at the same commit: 0 tap-target fails, 0 contrast fails.

The accessibility pass this waiver was written to cover actually worked, and here is what it moved, each measured per selector over CDP with the cache disabled rather than inferred from a report:

  a.chip2 node and skill links      23.75px tall  ->  44px
  .syl-t a post-title links            17px tall  ->  44px
  .part-head .ask            21px tall, 1.56:1    ->  44px, about 5.8:1
  .tnode .nm label, light theme           1.35:1  ->  14.73:1
  .gb-seal 'foundations', light theme     2.92:1  ->  12.56:1
  .arm-chip.on                            1.05:1  ->  8.31:1 in both themes

The board geometry freeze was respected and verified three ways: no layout property appears in any board hunk, getBoundingClientRect for all 16 .tnode/.frame/.nm boxes is byte-identical between pre-fix and post-fix runs, and 390px screenshots in both themes show only label text becoming readable. Every board change is a color property.

WHY IT IS STILL WAIVED. max_warn is 0 and the report carries 361 warnings, dominated by 314 'text too small on a phone' entries. That is a deliberate typographic register in DESIGN.md, not a defect backlog, and 0 is not a threshold anyone has argued for against this app's actual type scale. 34 target warns and 5 contrast warns sit above the WCAG floor in the comfortable band. Setting a defensible max_warn, or splitting the warn budget by kind, is the real work here and it is a design decision rather than a bug fix.

Not fixed, deliberately, and named so it is not lost: the primary .finish-day button gradient has the same --gold/--gold-hi theme-inversion problem that .arm-chip.on had. The codebase's own comment says it needs a --btn-face pass with a screenshot review under DESIGN.md, not a token edit bundled into an a11y sweep, and that precedent was followed.

RENEWED 2026-08-24 WITH A NAMED CLOSE PATH INSTEAD OF A DATE SLIP. Operator decision this date: the repo migrates to a Bun toolchain (bun build with the HTML entrypoint, Workbox, TypeScript strict) with Playwright as the e2e lane. That decision dissolves this waiver's real blocker: CI e2e stops depending on the private claude-setup repo's flow.py entirely, because the Playwright suite is self-contained in this repo. The same suite doubles as the local fallback the operator asked for against GitHub Actions minutes exhaustion: one command runs it locally pre-push, CI is merely the remote copy. New expiry 2026-09-15 is the migration milestone, not a drift allowance; if the migration has not produced a Playwright step in ci.yml by then, this waiver is not renewed on this reasoning again. Everything in the prior reason about the confirm-only cmd needing deletion in the lifting commit still binds. PRIOR REASON KEPT BELOW.

Genuinely reduced on 2026-08-08, not renewed unchanged. CI now runs 38 of the 48 tests in tests/ (5 of 6 files: mentor.test.ts, decks.test.ts, contract.test.ts, fuzz.test.ts, mutation.test.ts), added as a new step in .github/workflows/ci.yml. All five read index.html and daemon/server_parse.ts directly (server_parse.ts has zero imports of its own) and open no network connection, so they run on any runner with no secret; verified locally at the pinned bun version (1.3.14) before this commit, 38 pass, 0 fail. That is a real coverage increase, not the whole unit domain: tests/boundaries.test.ts (10 tests) stays local-only, excluded on purpose rather than deleted from the suite. Its top-level await on the gitignored daemon/.key means the whole file fails to import without that file present, so no -t filter can rescue a subset in CI. Its 5 worker: tests need a real SYNC_KEY secret this repo does not have (`gh secret list` returns only CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN), and its 5 daemon: tests need a daemon process with its own Claude Agent SDK credential that no GitHub runner here starts. Adding either secret is a production-adjacent decision this waiver does not make for itself. The Chrome clause in the prior reason is retracted, not renewed, because it is now measured wrong: GitHub's own ubuntu-latest image ships Google Chrome 150.0.7871.128 with a CDP-capable driver (confirmed from actions/runner-images' Ubuntu2404 README), so 'needs a Chrome CDP endpoint' is no longer the blocker for e2e. The real remaining blocker for e2e, for the review domain, and for the gate's own primary path (gate.py run) is one fact, not three: flow.py, panel.py and gate.py all live in ShovalBenjer/claude-setup, confirmed private ('private':true via gh api). Running any of them here means either a new PAT secret scoped to a private admin repo used inside a PUBLIC repo's CI job, or vendoring those three files into daily-deep-learning, which is out of this task's edit scope and a separate content decision (claude-setup internals landing in a public repo). Neither happened here; both are real, named decisions, not a quick fix. Honesty note for the next reader: ci_runs_gate's fallback match checks only the LAST TOKEN of each contract cmd against the workflow text. unit's cmd ends in 'tests/', and the new CI step's command contains that substring, so the builtin will read unit as matched once this waiver lapses. It is covered for 5 of 6 files; tests/boundaries.test.ts is not, and this note exists so that substring match is never mistaken for full unit coverage. New expiry set to 2026-08-15 to align with the e2e and a11y_ux waivers in this same file, since all three now turn on the same claude-setup access decision, not because the date slipped.

Correction to the paragraph above, not a replacement: private repo access is not the only blocker for e2e, it is the first of two. Even with claude-setup readable from Actions, claude-setup/tools/browser/cdp.py's chrome_path() (lines 79 to 90) hardcodes three Windows-only paths and calls SystemExit if none exist, and launch() (lines 245 to 278) only reaches that Windows-only fallback after failing to adopt an already-listening debug port. So a GitHub runner having Chrome preinstalled does not help flow.py start it: a CI step would still need to launch Chrome itself with the remote-debugging flag first, which is unwritten work on top of the access decision, not a consequence of solving it. Also worth naming for the next reader: a new hermetic test file added to tests/ has to be added to the ci.yml step by name, the same way this contract's own unit domain once sat pinned to a single file and gated nothing new until it was widened; the CI step does not glob tests/, so it will not pick one up on its own.

pipeline._cmd_comment: This cmd exists only to produce the waived.confirm string above. The pipeline domain is still evaluated by builtin ci_runs_gate whenever it is NOT waived, and eval_domain checks builtin before cmd (gate.py:939 runs before :950), so this cmd never drives the real verdict while the waiver is live. It must be deleted, not left in place, in the same commit that lifts or removes the waiver: ci_runs_gate builds its own fallback token list from every domain that has a cmd (cmds = [d.get("cmd") for d in domains.values() if d.get("cmd")]), so once this domain is no longer short-circuited by waived, its own confirm-only cmd would be added to that list too, and the trailing whitespace-split token of this cmd (a literal quote character after the word CI) does not appear in any workflow file, which would fail the domain on its own confirm plumbing instead of on a real gap. Verified 2026-08-08: computed the trailing token of every OTHER domain's cmd in this contract and grepped it against the concatenated text of ci.yml, deploy.yml and claude-code-review.yml. build (tools/validate_links.py), unit (tests/), types (tools/gen_art.sh) and review (the literal ".") all match something in a workflow file. e2e (state/e2e/last.json) is the only one that does not, which is the exact and only real gap this waiver is about.
